plan.topic: Why a greasy or rich meal can hit harder on tirzepatide (slower stomach emptying), and gentler ways to eat it
plan.angle:
20:00 funnel Short and spin-off of L1, tight arm. It asks one fresh question rather than re-cutting the L1 script.
- Sentence 1: 'Greasy meal hit you harder on tirzepatide? There's a reason.'
- By 6 s, in label wording: tirzepatide delays gastric emptying, and nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea are common. Use one pooled rate per dose vs placebo, matching L1's verified script exactly.
- Advisory line at its exact scope: avoiding fatty or high-fibre foods in the first few days can help ease nausea.
- Untagged tips: a smaller portion, eat slowly, stop at comfortably full, sip fluids unless you've been told to limit them. No 'bad' foods, no guilt, no calorie talk.
- Emergency card: severe stomach pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting, means stop and call your healthcare provider right away. Then the scoped don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line and the closing line. No Exp F line.
- Post note: the related-video target is L1 once it's verified live, otherwise Side Effects.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide and Greasy Food: Why It Hits Harder #shorts
plan.why: Spin-off of L1, and it drives traffic to the long video. It's a felt symptom in a practical moment, and searches about rich-meal nausea build toward the Nov 20–28 holiday meals.

package.title: Tirzepatide: Why Greasy Meals May Hit Harder #shorts
package.description:
Tirzepatide slows stomach emptying, and experts say greasy meals may worsen nausea. Enjoying a rich meal? Take a smaller portion, eat slowly, and stop at comfortably full. No bad foods, no guilt.

Severe stomach pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting: stop and call your healthcare provider right away. For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.

Sources:
Zepbound Prescribing Information and Medication Guide (revised 28 Aug 2026): https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=487cd7e7-434c-4925-99fa-aa80b1cc776b
Gorgojo-Martínez et al., J Clin Med 2023 (published 24 Dec 2022): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9821052/

#tirzepatide #GLP1 #sideeffects
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
The Short is accurate and safe. It can ship once the two minor wording fixes below are applied.

**What I checked against the sources:**
- **Zepbound label (src1, revised 28 Aug 2026):**
  - Nausea is 25%, 29% and 28% on 5, 10 and 15 mg, against 8% on placebo. The data are pooled from Studies 1 and 2, over up to 72 weeks.
  - Vomiting and diarrhea are also among the most common reactions.
  - Section 12.2 says "Tirzepatide delays gastric emptying".
  - The Medication Guide's pancreatitis line says to stop and call your healthcare provider right away for severe stomach pain that will not go away, with or without vomiting. The script matches all of this.
- **Expert consensus (src2):** this is Gorgojo-Martínez et al., J Clin Med 2023;12(1):145, published 24 Dec 2022. It recommends:
  - low-fat, easy-to-digest food
  - "Avoid sweet meals"
  - "Eat smaller portions"
  - "Eat slowly"
  - stopping when you feel full
  - sipping fluids

  That supports s4 and s5.

**Other checks:**
- Narration is 157 words, within the standard arm and under 160.
- The safety lines come in the right order. The emergency line keeps "right away" and "with or without vomiting", and the don't-stop line is scoped.
- There is correctly no Exp F line, since this is the 20:00 Short.
- There is no body-shaming and no restrictive nudge. "No bad foods, no guilt" helps here.

**Minor issues:**
- s1 joins slower stomach emptying to greasy food with "so". Neither source states that link directly.
- s3's narration doesn't say which trials the numbers come from.

Neither fix pushes the word count over 160: total becomes 159.

issues.claim: Tirzepatide slows stomach emptying, so greasy meals can hit harder.
issues.problem: The 'so' turns an inference into a cause. The label only says tirzepatide delays gastric emptying, and adds that the delay is largest after the first dose and lessens over time. It's the expert consensus that advises low-fat food for GI symptoms. Neither source directly says greasy meals 'hit harder' because of slower emptying.
issues.fix: Replace sentence 1 with: "Tirzepatide slows stomach emptying, and experts say greasy meals may worsen nausea." Keep "You're not imagining it." This adds 2 words, so the total goes from 157 to 159.

issues.claim: Nausea hit twenty-five to twenty-nine percent across doses, versus eight percent on placebo. At least one in four.
issues.problem: Only the stat card's attribution names the population and timeframe. Spoken alone, the number sounds like it applies to everyone taking tirzepatide in any setting.
issues.fix: Replace "At least one in four." with "In the weight-loss trials." The word count stays the same. Keep the stat card attribution as it is.
